# cloider_dns_record (Resource)

A DNS record set of a custom `cloider_domain`: every value of one type at one name. The api keeps one record per type and name, so list all of a name's values in one resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cloider_domain" "example" {
  name = "example.com"
}

resource "cloider_dns_record" "www" {
  domain = cloider_domain.example.name
  type   = "A"
  name   = "www"
  values = ["203.0.113.10", "203.0.113.11"]
  ttl    = 3600
}

resource "cloider_dns_record" "mail" {
  domain = cloider_domain.example.name
  type   = "MX"
  values = ["10 mx1.example.net.", "20 mx2.example.net."]
  ttl    = 3600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The custom domain the record belongs to. Subdomains under Cloider's roots don't take records. Changing it replaces the record.
- `ttl` (Number) Seconds resolvers may cache the record, 60 to 172800.
- `type` (String) `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT`, `NS`, `CAA`, `HTTPS`, `SPF`, `SRV`, `PTR`.
- `values` (List of String) The record's values, such as IP addresses for `A` or `10 mail.example.com.` for `MX`. A `CNAME` takes one.

### Optional

- `name` (String) The name under the domain, such as `www`. Defaults to `""`, the domain itself.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The record's id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A record is imported by its id, see `cloider dns list example.com`
terraform import cloider_dns_record.www 1042
```
